proposed_title: The small policy experiment did not establish a benefit from longer instructions.
decision: Decide whether to supply concise rules, detailed boundary guidance, or no custom policy.
finding: The concise policy contains 219 instruction words; detailed guidance brings it to 438, and neutral filler to 450. Relative to detailed guidance, the short version loses source agreement on 2 of 12 cases for Luna decision API, 1 for Jev Choice and Claude, and 0 for the other four interfaces. No paired accuracy difference is statistically resolved.
implication: This supports testing policy examples and wording, but not a general claim that longer policies are better. Only 12 conversations are tested. Neutral filler and useful guidance are different interventions; withholding also removes option definitions.
exclusion_reason: Only 12 conversations; zero to two changes per model do not warrant a standalone chart or a general policy-length conclusion.

proposed_title: More answer choices did not establish better harm classification.
decision: Decide whether to ask for a binary action or a more detailed category.
finding: With the detailed policy fixed, expanding the answer choices changes at most one operational judgment per tested interface and condition on these 12 conversations. Category outputs are collapsed to safe/unsafe for comparison; there is no independent category-level human gold.
implication: A more detailed answer format is not evidence of better category identification. The actual offered lists contain 2, 3, 7, and 15 choices, including safe, caution, and catch-all labels. Keep the small diagnostic in supporting material rather than claiming a reliable gain from more choices.
exclusion_reason: Only 12 conversations and at most one change per model/condition; keep a short limitation paragraph.
